topics.topic: Clock-sampling policy for session operations, including using one upload-arrival reading for validity and idle refresh
questions: Does an upload take one monotonic reading at that arrival and use that same value both to decide validity and to update `last_request`, or may those operations take separate readings?

Does Registry take exactly one monotonic-clock reading when the head completes and use that same value both to check every session limit and to set `last_request`, or may those decisions use separate readings?

How many monotonic and UTC readings does each sign-in, ordinary owner request, confirmation show or submission, sign-out, and cleanup pass take, and are all decisions and timestamps within one operation derived from one captured reading?

quotes:
Every request is checked at its arrival, and only then — the reading of
`clock.monotonic_reading` this operation takes when it is called, which for
an upload is after its bounded head has been read (A13 rule 2): a session that has
reached 8 hours from sign-in or 30 minutes without a request, or is marked
signed out, serves no request; a change carries the CSRF value of its
session, compared in constant time (A13 rule 5).

At its arrival a request carrying a valid session restarts the session's
30 minutes, whatever its answer — a CSRF refusal included; of concurrent
arrivals the latest counts (A13 rule 2). A sign-out's admission marks the
session signed out at once.

The pass alone
ends sessions by their limits: it takes the import lock, reads
`clock.monotonic_reading` once, and decides every session by that one
reading, in the order of their sign-in, each under its own lock, so the
order decides nothing.
judgement.why: The later owner-session operations fix the admission reading, use that arrival to refresh idle time, and separately specify the readings taken by confirmation and cleanup operations.

topics.topic: Refusal behavior, state effects, and failure precedence for malformed or oversized upload heads
questions: What happens when the multipart head is malformed, has no file boundary, or exceeds `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` before it can be completely read, and which A04 failure stage supplies the answer when the upload has not yet reached its defined arrival?

What must Registry do when the file part has not begun after `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` bytes, and does that refusal leave the session, idle deadline, pending confirmation, and previously uploaded file unchanged?

For an upload, which refusal wins when the session is invalid and the multipart head is malformed, too large, or does not place the CSRF field before the file, given that A13 requires reading that head before the session check?

quotes:
The CSRF value the first part carries, the delimiter that ends the file
part, and the file part's declared length — the request's declared length
less the head it read and the closing delimiter with its final `--` and line
end, or none when the request declared none; or that the head is not of that form — no multipart content type or
boundary, a first part that is not the CSRF field, no second part that is
the file — or is longer than the imported `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES`
constant, or declares less than that head and the closing delimiter, or the
request's stream fails or ends while the head is read — with none of these
values.

None: a head of another form answers no CSRF value, and the upload is
refused at stage (1) as a change without one (A04 rule 6, A13 rule 5).

Reads the stream up to the start of the file part's content and no further,
at most the bound; a head it refuses leaves the rest of the stream unread.
None: it reads the request's stream only.
judgement.why: The later upload-framing operation enumerates malformed, overlong and prematurely ended heads, maps them to a missing-CSRF stage-(1) refusal, and gives the bounded read no state impact.

topics.topic: Which request-local or shared state may be retained while reading the bounded upload head
questions: What does “no state held” forbid: shared session state or locks, retained request-local header and CSRF values, buffered multipart-head bytes, or all of these?
What kind of state is forbidden during the bounded head read, given that Registry must parse multipart framing and retain the CSRF value long enough to perform the stage-1 CSRF check?
What state is forbidden before upload admission: session state, uploaded file bytes, the multipart head, parser state, the CSRF value, or every per-request value?

judgement.why: This is the same request-local multipart-head retention question already decided by P3, and the quoted passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Meaning and required disposal timing of multipart head data that is “never kept”
quotes:
A13 rule 7: the CSRF value is taken from the form's body, never from a URL,
and is neither checked nor kept here — `owner_sessions` checks it at the
session check. A19 rule 4 stays `migration_import`'s: no byte of the file is
read here, and the file part's stream, a `MultipartFileBody` over the same
stream and that delimiter, gives the file's bytes only as its reader asks.
None: it reads the request's stream only.

`UploadBody`'s one implementation is
  `MultipartFileBody(stream, delimiter)`, `policy`, owned by
  `upload_framing`: it gives the file part's bytes and ends before the
  delimiter, holding in memory no more than the delimiter's length of
  look-ahead, so `_parse_export` still receives the bare JSON object.
precedent.why: The later texts prohibit retained upload-framing state, permit only bounded parsing and delimiter look-ahead, and assign no state impact to reading the head.

topics.topic: Exact byte extent of the bounded multipart head and treatment of required fields absent within it
questions: Which bytes constitute the bounded head: HTTP request headers, multipart preamble and boundaries, the CSRF part, the file part's headers, and any bytes immediately preceding the file content?

Exactly which bytes constitute the head, what happens when the file part or CSRF field is not found within the maximum, and at what instant such a malformed or oversized-head request is deemed to arrive?

quotes:
`upload_framing.read_upload_head` reads the head alone,
  at most `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` (8192 bytes) — the boundary from the
  content type, the CSRF part, the file part's headers — and answers
  `UploadHead`: the CSRF value, the delimiter `\r\n--<boundary>` that ends
  the file part, and the file part's declared length — the request's
  declared length less the head read and the closing delimiter with its
  final `--\r\n` — or none of them.

Reads the stream up to the start of the file part's content and no further,
at most the bound; a head it refuses leaves the rest of the stream unread.

A
head of another form gives no CSRF value, and the upload is refused at stage
(1) before any byte of the file is read. An upload arrives, for the session
check, once its head has been read (A13 rule 2).
judgement.why: The later contracts enumerate the head's exact multipart components and specify that a head missing the required form within the bound is refused before admission and without reading file bytes.

topics.topic: Representation, units, precision, ordering, and overflow behavior of monotonic session times
questions: In what concrete representation and unit are monotonic readings, stored session instants and deadlines carried and compared?
In what representation are monotonic readings and stored session deadlines held, including their unit, precision, ordering and overflow behavior?

quotes:
Every duration in this decision — the 8 hours, the 30, 15 and 10
   minutes, the 60 seconds — is measured by the process's monotonic clock,
   which a change of the wall clock does not move and which counts the time
   the host or its VM was suspended, so a session does not outlive a
   suspension; instants Registry records
   and the 03:00 of A18 are UTC wall-clock time.
judgement.why: The monotonic representation question concerns an unchanged passage, and the upload-arrival change did not make that representation question matter.

topics.topic: Required test covering upload arrival at idle or absolute session limits
questions: Which Required tests item must show the new upload-arrival rule—especially that an upload whose head begins before the idle limit but completes at or after it is refused, while one whose head completes just before it is served?

Which Required tests item must show that an upload begun before an idle or eight-hour limit but whose head finishes at or after the limit is refused, while one whose head finishes just before it is admitted?

judgement.why: This asks which Required test must demonstrate the upload-arrival boundary, the same State 8 test-handoff question already judged in P15.

precedent.topic: Required-test coverage for multipart head, framing, ordering, and pre-read size enforcement
quotes:
An import file of exactly 50 × 1024 × 1024 bytes, sent by the upload form
   with its CSRF field first, is read; one of a byte more is refused, with
   no mapping shown, also when its declared length is smaller or absent, and
   the file the session kept before stays kept.
precedent.why: The question asks which executable checks demonstrate or bind the stated upload properties, which the transition rules assign to the State 8 test handoff rather than reopening State 2.

topics.topic: Whether owner-session cookies are always HTTPS-only or conditionally so for remote access
questions: Is the owner-session cookie always marked Secure and therefore never sent over local HTTP, or is HTTPS-only conditional on access from another machine?
Is the owner-session cookie always marked and handled as HTTPS-only, including local access, or is HTTPS-only required only when the interface is reached from another machine as A13 rule 1 states?

quotes:
The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner
   session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over
   HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only
   to Registry's own origin.

the session cookie is always
HTTPS-only, which is stricter than A13 rule 1.
judgement.why: Both cookie passages are unchanged in the closed and current texts, and the upload-arrival change did not make their difference matter.

topics.topic: Agent-session access-version initialization, required presentation, and stale or absent version refusal
questions: What is an AgentSession's initial access version, which actions must state it, and what exact refusal and precedence apply when the stated version is stale or absent?

topics.topic: Agent-session termination events and post-termination retention policy
questions: What events end an agent session, and is its record deleted, retained permanently, or retained for a defined period after it ends?

topics.topic: Audit policy and entry contents for refused agent attempts and authority reads
questions: Which refused attempts, if any, write audit entries, and what subject, outcome and safe detail does each such entry contain?
Do agent-authority reads or their refusals ever write audit entries, and if so which ones?

topics.topic: Handling and timeout policy for stalled, disconnected, or prematurely ended upload-head reads
questions: If the peer stalls, disconnects, or ends the multipart body before the complete head is read, when and how is the request refused, and is there a read deadline?

quotes:
Validity is
   checked when a request arrives (A04 rule 6, stage 1) — an upload, whose
   form sends its CSRF value before its file (A19 rule 4), arrives when that
   head, at most the imported `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` constant, has been
   read (owner, 2026-11-17); a request that
   passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs, and
   a restart that interrupts it leaves nothing of it (A04 rule 4).

The upload is the file the owner
   interface's form sends as the second part of a multipart body, after the
   field that carries the CSRF value (A13 rules 5, 7; owner, 2026-11-17): the
   limit and every byte this rule counts are the file part's, never the
   form's framing.
judgement.divergence: One implementation waits indefinitely for a stalled pre-file head, retaining connection and parser resources; another applies a read deadline and terminates the request, which the caller and operator observe.
judgement.why: The texts define arrival only after the bounded head is read but set no deadline or stalled-read termination rule before that point.

witness.initial: A valid owner session is one minute from its idle limit.
events: A caller sends an upload request carrying that session and begins the CSRF multipart part.
The caller stops sending before the file part's headers complete.
outcomes: Registry waits indefinitely, retaining the connection and bounded parser state while the session becomes invalid separately.
Registry reaches a read deadline, refuses or closes the request, and releases its connection and parser resources.
witness.observer: The caller observes completion versus no completion, and the operator observes different resource retention.
basis: The owner uploads the export file (R0-72) in the owner interface.

The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner
   session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over
   HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only
   to Registry's own origin.

topics.topic: Integer value of UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES
questions: What integer byte value does `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` have?

judgement.why: This is exactly the numeric-value question already decided by P5, and the relevant texts have not changed.

quotes:
`upload_framing.read_upload_head` reads the head alone,
  at most `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` (8192 bytes) — the boundary from the
  content type, the CSRF part, the file part's headers — and answers
  `UploadHead`: the CSRF value, the delimiter `\r\n--<boundary>` that ends
  the file part, and the file part's declared length — the request's
  declared length less the head read and the closing delimiter with its
  final `--\r\n` — or none of them.
precedent.why: The State 6 contract fixes the limit at 8192 bytes and enumerates the boundary, CSRF part, and file-part headers as the bounded head.

topics.topic: Required test for revision increments and last_changed timestamp consistency
questions: Which Required tests item must show that every accepted revision-moving change increments by exactly one and writes `last_changed` from the operation's decided current-time reading?

topics.topic: Required test for service classification ceilings and Cabinet Kernel's exact highest class
questions: Which Required tests item must show that no accepted answer exceeds a service's highest class and that Cabinet Kernel's highest class is exactly `business_confidential`, rather than merely showing denial of particular operations?

topics.topic: Required test proving stored values cannot become executable syntax
questions: Which Required tests item must demonstrate that stored values cannot become query, command, template or other executable syntax, beyond being stored and read back unchanged?

topics.topic: Synchronization between request admission and concurrent session cleanup or sign-out
questions: What prevents a cleanup pass or sign-out from ending and removing a session after another request passes the session check but before that request takes the session lock, and what state must the admitted request then operate on?

quotes:
A request that passed
completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs or waits (A13
rule 2). After the check, a change that touches no uploaded file takes its
place on the session's lock at once; a request that touches one first waits
for the import lock and then takes its place, so the locks are always taken
import first and no place on a session's lock waits for the import lock (A16
rule 2). A request asks for the import lock when it is admitted. The import
lock is granted in the order requests asked for it, and
the session's lock in the order places were taken, and the session's
changes apply one at a time in that order (A13 rule 2: "in the order in
which they take the session's one lock").

Its turn on a session's lock comes after every change
of the session admitted before the pass began, which completes first with
the confirmation and the upload it may need (A13 rule 2).
judgement.why: The later session API reserves lock order at admission and requires cleanup and sign-out to follow already-admitted changes, preserving the state those changes need.

topics.topic: Whether all import-created records and audit data share one transaction UTC instant
questions: What is the import's instant, how many UTC readings does the import transaction take, and must every new Customer, the migration closure and the import audit entry carry the same instant?

quotes:
A Customer the import makes is
  created at the import's instant with revision 1.
judgement.why: The import-instant question concerns an unchanged State 1 passage, and the upload-arrival change did not affect the transaction's UTC instant.

provenance.quote: A Customer the import makes is created at the import's instant with revision 1.

topics.topic: Whether an expired session is destroyed immediately or only during cleanup
questions: Does reaching a time limit end the session and destroy its state immediately, or only make it invalid until the next cleanup pass ends it and destroys its state?

quotes:
A session that has reached a
   limit serves no request from that
   moment: a request carrying it is refused at the session check. Registry
   ends it — and drops its pending confirmation and its uploaded file with it
   (M11) — at a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the
   start; the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import
   lock and then each session's lock (A16 rule 2) and deciding under them.
judgement.why: The distinction between immediate invalidity and destruction at the next pass is stated in an unchanged passage and was not made material by the upload-arrival change.

topics.topic: Whether concurrent upload validity and idle refresh are ordered by arrival or lock/check order
questions: When concurrent requests finish their heads in chronological order but execute their session checks or acquire the session lock in the opposite order, must validity and idle refresh be linearized by arrival time or by check/lock order?

quotes:
At its arrival a request carrying a valid session restarts the session's
30 minutes, whatever its answer — a CSRF refusal included; of concurrent
arrivals the latest counts (A13 rule 2).

Every request is checked at its arrival, and only then — the reading of
`clock.monotonic_reading` this operation takes when it is called, which for
an upload is after its bounded head has been read (A13 rule 2): a session that has
reached 8 hours from sign-in or 30 minutes without a request, or is marked
signed out, serves no request; a change carries the CSRF value of its
session, compared in constant time (A13 rule 5).

Every request is checked
at its arrival; a change, or any request touching an uploaded file, then
takes its place on the session's lock — the latter after waiting for the
import lock, granted in the order requests asked for it — and the session's
lock is granted in the order places were taken (A13 rule 2, A16 rule 2).
judgement.why: The later texts make validity and idle refresh use each request's arrival reading, with the latest concurrent arrival retained independently of the subsequent lock order.

topics.topic: Whether erasure date, cutoff, and audit instant derive from one UTC reading
questions: Are “today,” the cutoff and the erasure entry's current instant derived from one UTC reading, or may the operation read UTC more than once across midnight?

quotes:
The date of an erasure is a date not later than today, the current date in
   UTC; a later date is refused. Every entry whose instant is before 00:00 UTC
   of that date is removed.

The erasure's own entry is written after the removal, in the same
   transaction, with the current instant; it is therefore never removed by the
   erasure that wrote it.
judgement.why: The audit-erasure timing passages are unchanged in the closed and current texts, and the upload-arrival change did not make the midnight-reading question matter.

topics.topic: Whether the A13 upload change requires a new recorded browser-boundary security review
questions: Was the A13 change also reviewed under `browser_boundary`, which names A13 and which rule 2 therefore reopens, or must that category be reviewed and recorded now?
